Model/effort: Claude Opus 5.5, max effort as set by the workflow harness (not verifiable from inside the run), so it ran outside the verified calibrated setting; autonomous run, brief taken as given (seasoned practitioner, publication, house style per prompt). (5) explore #1, U06 padas 1–3: quotations only (4024, 4025, Buton, Tsongkhapa, Changkya). (6) segment KK-07:3669 (Kongtrul's Uttaratantra commentary): the verse is the supreme nirmanakaya's display of the twelve deeds. (7) segment KK-07:3699: gloss of the stanza ('jig rten mkhyen = ji snyed mkhyen pa'i ye shes; the first birth = the Tushita birth; the descent = first deed). (8) meta KK-07: Kongtrul, Karma Kamtsang series.
- Resumed session: (9) explore #2, U07 padas 1–3: quotations only; surfaced Jamyang Lodrö's Uttaratantra commentary (Sakya). (10–11) segment PARCHIN-094:7553 and :7578 + meta: its gloss is Kongtrul's nearly verbatim (compassion as cause; extent- and nature-knowledge; Tushita birth as the god Tokkar). (12) explore #3, U10 sources clause: returned only this commentary (BO_EGS_0002:99, :101) and two aligned segments of an existing English translation of U10 (EN_EGS_0005:55–56); no gloss; exposure logged, nothing used, U10's readings were fixed in Pass 1; further explore on the commentator's own prose dropped (prompt rule 3). (14–15) segment PARCHIN-094:7603 and :7624: the palace deed with several consorts, so "his circle of queens" stands.

Rough shares of the resumed session: ~15% re-establishing state after the interruption (run files, eight saved tool outputs, the skill and nine reference files re-read), ~5% tool outputs (two explore, six segment, two meta, MITRA, beats.py), ~70% reasoning (grounding decisions on Q10/Q11, MITRA triage, the verse loop, restructuring U10, the check), ~10% writing the sketch additions, glossary, pass-3 text and this file.

**Problems in the skill text:**
1. Non-blind examples. grounding.md §3 (example 1), notes.md §4 (output sample), english.md §9 (#17–#19) and tibetan-verse SKILL.md §2 ("as in the Uttaratantra's twelve deeds") are built on this very page (U05, U06, U10, U12). notes.md §4 even gives a finished U06 footnote and a Comm line citing Toh 4025 118b, KHEZ009:4568 and EGS_0004:3495, none of which this run saw in a hit; copying it would break grounding.md §4's honesty rule. V1 no longer measures v2 blind.
2. Explore surfaces the existing translation. SKILL.md §4.2 and grounding.md §1 send explore on the text's own words, but dm.py explore has no exclude, and for a work indexed with an aligned English version (BO_EGS_0002 + EN_EGS_0005) it returns the passage and its published English. identify's --exclude takes only a Toh number, which sungbum texts lack. Neither file says what to do with an EN_ hit (cite, ignore, report).
3. Own-prose units. "At least once for the page's central passage" (SKILL.md §4.2) does not fit a page whose central passage is the author's own homage: nothing in the canon glosses it. The header's grounding field (SKILL.md §8) offers only "… gloss followed" / "none found", and grounding.md §4 adds only "service unavailable"; there is no value for "not queried".
4. A verse sentence across units. SKILL.md §8 and notes.md §4 want one HEADER/TEXT per unit, but tibetan-verse §3 works per sentence (prose first, permute inside the sentence, one mode/kind/measure line per block). With the verb in pada 15 (U09) of a sentence starting in U06, the order declaration and the block line have no per-unit home. Neither file says how to split a verse sentence across unit blocks.
5. Footnotes from sources vs the seasoned column. notes.md §2 rule 2 allows footnotes only from the Tibetan of a commentary or source read, never from memory. Its seasoned column invites "an enumeration" (here the five certainties, ten powers, four fearlessnesses), but no grounding call covers these, so the footnotes the column asks for cannot be written.
6. TITLE row format undocumented in the text. SKILL.md §2 gives the glossary as wylie/English/note with TITLE rows "in the same file"; tibetan-citations §4 lists the fields without an order. Only register.py's docstring fixes TITLE/english/wylie/iast/locator. The Pass-1 session put the Wylie in the English column, which register.py --titles reads as the English title.
7. prose.md is still v1. Its heading says "Pass 2, prose units", while in v2 drafting is Pass 1 and style Pass 3. Its §4 step 1 asks for a "construal object (analysis.md)" for every unit, against SKILL.md §3.2 (the full schema only for contested units).
8. The MITRA line. SKILL.md §4.4 says "One MITRA: line in the notes" (per page?); notes.md §1 makes MITRA: a per-unit tag "only where there is something to say".
9. The band for a thin pada. guidelines.md §2 tolerates a spread of three only "when the padas are long". Yet §5 says "a thin pada stays short", SKILL.md §2 asks enumerative runs for "the wider measure", and beats.py passes 2–4 as OK for 7-syllable padas. For "he takes birth" (2 beats, nothing may be added) the letter of §2 cannot be met.
10. beats.py UNKNOWN. tibetan-verse SKILL.md §3.7 says to add unknown words to tools/lexicon.py, which means editing the skill under test during a test run ("descends" was missing). This run patched it at runtime from a scratchpad wrapper instead.
11. No resume protocol. SKILL.md §1 reads some references "once per session" (english.md) and others "once per project" (modes.md, notes.md). After a context reset it is unclear which must be re-read, so this run re-read everything it applied. Nor does the skill say which state files make a run resumable (here the sketch, glossary, draft and saved dm outputs sufficed).

text: Accordingly, in the *Sublime Continuum* it is said:
Out of great compassion, knowing the world,
he looks upon all the worlds,
and then, never stirring from the dharmakaya,
through emanations of many kinds

footnotes.text: The commentaries explain this as his wisdom that knows the world in all its extent, with which he looks upon every world of beings he is to guide. Never stirring from the dharmakaya is his wisdom that knows things as they are, which all the while rests in unchanging equipoise. Great compassion, the wish to take every being into his care, is the reason he displays the deeds.

notes.text: Toh 4024 (theg pa chen po rgyud bla ma'i bstan bcos), D 64b-15–18, verbatim (identify: 28 syllables); witness Toh 4025 (vyākhyā), D 118b-31; quoted also by Buton (ACIP S12060E:3406), Tsongkhapa (ACIP S5281E:14969), Changkya (ACIP S0063M_T:4453); 68 parallels, no sense variant in these padas. Register row V1/U06-U09.

Kongtrul, rgyud bla ma'i 'grel pa phyir mi ldog pa seng ge'i nga ro (KK-07:3690–3696) and Jamyang Lodrö, nges don rab gsal snang ba (Sakya; PARCHIN-094:7568–7573) give the same gloss nearly word for word: thugs rje chen pos = the cause of the displaying (rgyu gang las ston na … thugs rje chen pos rjes su bzung bar bzhed pa'i rgyu las); 'jig rten mkhyen = 'jig rten gyi khams ji snyed pa mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyis … gzigs (the extent-knowledge as the means of the looking); chos kyi sku las ma g.yos = ji lta ba mkhyen pa'i ye shes in unchanging equipoise, nam yang ma g.yos; followed.

resolved by both commentaries for the verbal reading: 'jig rten mkhyen = "knowing the world" (Pass 1 had the epithet "the Knower of the World", lokavid); thugs rje chen pos as the cause, "out of great compassion"; 'jig rten kun = "all the worlds".

U06 GROUNDING: Kongtrul, rgyud bla ma'i 'grel pa phyir mi ldog pa seng ge'i nga ro (KK-07:3689–3696) and 'Jam dbyangs blo gros, nges don rab gsal snang ba (Sakya; PARCHIN-094:7568–7573) give the same gloss nearly word for word: thugs rje chen pos = the cause of the displaying (rgyu gang las ston na … thugs rje chen pos rjes su bzung bar bzhed pa'i rgyu las); 'jig rten mkhyen = 'jig rten gyi khams ji snyed pa mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyis (the wisdom knowing the world-realms in their extent), with which he looks upon all the worlds of disciples (gdul byar gyur pa'i 'jig rten ma lus pa kun); chos kyi sku las ma g.yos par = never (nam yang) stirring from equipoise in the unchanging dharmakaya, the wisdom knowing the nature (ji lta ba mkhyen pa'i ye shes); sprul pa'i rang bzhin sna tshogs kyis … ston = through manifold emanations he displays the twelve deeds; "ston" at the end governs the whole list (ston zhes 'og nas 'byung ba gsal byed du sbyar).
Followed: Q10 resolved by the two commentaries for the verbal branch: 'jig rten mkhyen = knowing the world (not the bare epithet "the Knower of the World"); thugs rje chen pos = "out of great compassion" (cause, scoping over the sentence); 'jig rten kun = all the worlds. Grammar permits it (verse drops the connective after mkhyen; the subject is the elided Buddha, as in the gloss's bdag nyid chen po des).
MITRA U06: "he knows the world" agrees with the commentaries (the change is made on the gloss, not on MITRA).

The verse you provided is a famous citation from the **Mahāyānottaratantraśāstra** (The Treatise on the Sublime Continuum of the Great Vehicle), traditionally attributed to the Bodhisattva Maitreya. It describes the nature of the Buddha's Emanation Body (*nirmāṇakāya*), which manifests various deeds to benefit sentient beings without ever departing from the Ultimate Reality (*dharmakāya*).

In the Dharmamitra Database, this specific verse is cited across numerous Tibetan commentaries and treatises to explain the "Twelve Deeds" of a Buddha or the inconceivable nature of a Buddha's activities.

footnotes.text: The commentaries explain this first birth as his birth as a god in the Tushita heaven, where he brought a great many gods to ripening and liberation. It is the ground of the deeds, the first of which is his descent from Tushita to Jambudvipa.

notes.text: KK-07:3697–3698 and PARCHIN-094:7574–7576: skye ba mngon par skye ba = his taking birth (mngon par skye ba'i tshul bstan) as the holy god Tokkar (lha'i skye ba dam pa tog dkar) in Tushita, where he set many gods in ripening and liberation; Kongtrul calls it the ground of the deeds (mdzad pa'i gzhi) and counts the descent from Tushita to Jambudvipa as the first of the twelve; followed: one item, "takes birth", the explanation in the footnote.
resolved by the two commentaries (one item, the birth in Tushita); the Pass 1 placeholder "birth after birth" and the two-item reading (former births + rebirth) dropped: no gloss supports them.

explore.summary:
The phrase you provided refers to the "Twelve Deeds" of a Buddha, specifically the stages of taking birth. This sequence is a famous quotation from the **Mahāyānottaratantraśāstra** (also known as the *Ratnagotravibhāga* or *Gyü Lama*), attributed to Maitreya. It describes how a Buddha, while never wavering from the Dharmakāya, manifests through various emanations to guide sentient beings.

The specific lines you queried—"taking birth, descending from the Tuṣita heaven, and entering the womb"—are part of a larger verse describing the Nirmanakāya's activities.

reads mdzad rnams as the subject ("Those who have passed into nirvana manifest as remaining …") and yongs su ma dag as "entirely impure"; rejected: no agentive, and srid pa ji srid gnas par = for as long as existence remains.

units.mitra: Those who have passed into *nirvāṇa* manifest as remaining within the entirely impure realms for as long as cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*) endures; thus it was said.

text: Second. The supreme Sage conquered the four maras: the aggregates, the lord of death, the son of the gods and the afflictions. His scriptures are free from the extremes of permanence and annihilation and as immeasurable as the ocean's depths. This treatise was condensed from their sutras and tantras, from the treatises of Nagarjuna, Asanga and others, and from the meaning of the great Dharma Lord Drikungpa's profound pith instructions, worthy of honor like a naga king's crown jewel. It is free of the stains of not understanding, misunderstanding and doubt. Just as every need and wish comes forth when one prays to the vaidurya, the finest of gems, it fulfills every aim, temporary and ultimate. It is the *Heart of the Teaching*, which sets out the three—ground, path and fruition—and I shall explain it.

units.mitra: As for the second: I shall elucidate the heart of the treatise that teaches the ground, the path, and the result, which accomplishes all temporary and ultimate purposes, just as the supreme of all jewels, the vaiḍūrya, grants all needs and desires when supplicated. This work, which summarizes the profound meaning of the scriptures of the Supreme Sage—who has conquered the four māras, namely the aggregates, the Lord of Death, the son of the gods, and the afflictions, and whose teachings are free from the extremes of eternalism and nihilism and are as immeasurable as the depths of the ocean—as well as the sutras, tantras, the treatises of Nāgārjuna, Asaṅga, and others, and the profound pith instructions of the great Chöje Drikungpa, which are worthy of veneration like the crown jewel of the king of nāgas, has been compiled free from the stains of non-understanding, misunderstanding, and doubt.
